note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: Constant lower abdominal (suprapubic, midline) pain.
- Onset/duration: Began a few days ago; progressively worsening; severity ~8/10.
- Character/location: Midline, below the umbilicus; present all the time; worsens at times.
- Associated symptoms: Light pink vaginal bleeding/spotting; slight vaginal discharge; nausea without vomiting; constipation last week (about 1 week) now resolved; eating and drinking normally; able to do daily activities but pain is very uncomfortable.
- Gynecologic: Sexually active (last intercourse ~4 days ago). Contraceptive implant (Implanon) inserted ~1 year ago. Periods occur but timing is irregular on implant. Last menstrual period ~2–3 weeks ago; last period described as normal. No prior pregnancies. Last pregnancy test about 1 month ago (not since onset of pain).
- Urinary: Denies problems passing urine; denies pain or strong odor. Urinary frequency/change unclear.
- Constitutional/other negatives: Denies fever, feeling feverish, dyspnea, shoulder pain, or feeling faint.
- GI: No diarrhea reported; constipation last week, now improved; current stools described as normal. Blood in stool not confirmed.
- Travel: Last travel abroad ~1 year ago.
- Social: School teacher. Lives with husband and husband’s family. Recreational drugs denied. Smoking and alcohol use not recorded.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic conditions: Not reported.
- Surgical history: None reported.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Medications: Contraceptive implant (Implanon); other medications not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- General: No acute red flag symptoms reported (no syncope, no dyspnea).
- Abdomen: Not examined (teleconsultation).
- Pelvic exam: Not performed.
- Other systems: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Acute, worsening suprapubic abdominal pain with intermenstrual spotting in a sexually active 23-year-old using a contraceptive implant; pregnancy status unknown.
- Top differential considerations (consistent with transcript):
  - Ectopic pregnancy: Must be excluded given pelvic pain and spotting with no pregnancy test since symptom onset.
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): Pelvic pain with light bleeding and slight discharge; afebrile does not exclude.
  - Functional/hemorrhagic ovarian cyst: Can cause acute pelvic pain and irregular bleeding; implant use may be associated.
  - Appendicitis less likely but considered due to worsening pain and nausea without classic localization.

Management Plan:
- Arrange in-person evaluation for abdominal (and likely pelvic) examination via support line (patient to call and schedule).
- Perform a urine pregnancy test today; if positive, seek immediate medical care and call back urgently.
- Safety net: If pain worsens significantly, new severe symptoms develop, or unable to keep fluids down, seek urgent care/emergency evaluation.
- Symptom monitoring while awaiting appointment.

Patient Summary:
- A 23-year-old woman with several days of constant, worsening suprapubic pain, light pink spotting, and mild nausea. She has an Implanon in place and last pregnancy test was a month ago. Plan is in-person evaluation and a pregnancy test today to urgently rule out ectopic pregnancy.

Key Takeaways:
- Do a urine pregnancy test today; call back immediately if positive.
- Arrange a face-to-face appointment for examination as discussed.
- Seek urgent care if symptoms escalate, you develop faintness, severe shoulder pain, heavy bleeding, fever, or persistent vomiting.

Next Steps:
- Complete same-day urine pregnancy test.
- Attend scheduled in-person assessment for abdominal/pelvic exam.
- Further investigations to be guided by in-person findings (e.g., urinalysis, STI swabs, pelvic ultrasound) if indicated.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; full medication list; detailed menstrual history; complete sexual history (partners, protection, STI history); abdominal and pelvic exam findings; urine pregnancy test result; urinalysis; STI testing; imaging if indicated; smoking/alcohol history clarification.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Several unclear/inaudible segments; some responses ambiguous (e.g., urinary frequency, alcohol/smoking).
